title: 2026-02-18-open-model-picklist-integration-demo-cinderpoint
header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Mora (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Redwood Product); Marta Ruiz (CTO, CinderPoint), Ethan Cole (ML Platform), Priyanka Menon (Security), Samir Patel (Eng)
Shared artifacts: Redwood demo deck, model-catalog-sample.csv, benchmark-summary-spreadsheet (link placeholder)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked CinderPoint through the Model Catalog picklist, integration points in the Console and API, and Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization. Customer focused on selecting open models for a document-summarization product with strict PII controls and latency SLOs. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs and next steps to run a small bench sprint and share security docs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Mora: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, for the 30-ish minute demo — we actually have about 40 minutes scheduled so we can dig into questions. Marta, you good?
[00:18] Marta Ruiz: Yep thanks Alex, excited. We're evaluating open models for a new doc summarization flow and wanted to see how Redwood's catalog and benchmarks can speed that up.
[00:34] Alex Mora: Great. Quick intros — Priya is our systems SE who runs the bench sprints and Daniel's product — they'll demo the Console picklist and the Optimize suggestions.
[00:51] Priya Shah: Hi all. I'll start with the catalog. So what you see in the Console is a curated list of open models, each with a compatibility matrix — hardware rows (A100, H100, CPU int8), typical token throughput, and quality signals from our evals. The picklist lets you filter by task, sequence length, latency band, and privacy-friendly quantization profiles.
[01:22] [screen share sound / brief silence]
[01:30] Samir Patel: Quick question, when you say quality signals — is that MMLU-like or do you run custom evals?
[01:38] Priya Shah: Good q. We provide standard bench signals like MMLU/LLM-eval suites for general understanding, but importantly we attach your workload bench results when we run a sprint. So the compatibility matrix will show both "catalog-level" and "workload-level" results.
[01:55] Ethan Cole: And you run KV-cache measurements for long-document summarization? Because that matters for our 8k-20k token windows.
[02:04] Priya Shah: Yes, we measure effective KV throughput and memory footprint for typical prefix/streaming patterns. For your 12k median case we can flag models with efficient KV behaviour and note if they need FP16 vs quantized runtimes.
[02:22] [00:02:22] Marta: How do we integrate that into our CI — we don't want manual steps each time a model update lands.
[02:31] Daniel Kim: The API supports version pinning and model aliases. In the Console you can define a route that pins to a model family, then in CI you reference the route. When we publish new model variants you can opt into a canary or auto-fallback policy in the same route.
[02:46] [02:46] Priyanka Menon: From security perspective: KMS, audit logs, and data residency — we need to know PII never leaves our VPC.
[02:58] Alex Mora: Totally. For private deployments we provide a customer-managed control plane — KMS/HSM support, and we can restrict logs via retention policies. For hosted API we do retain audit logs but you can opt for Dedicated or Private which gives you full network isolation. We'll send the SOC2 + ISO docs after this.
[03:20] Priyanka: Please, yes. Also SSO for engineers and RBAC for token scoping.
[03:28] Alex Mora: We support SAML SSO and fine-grained API token scoping in the Console.
[03:34] [03:34] Samir: Back to models — some of our edge cases need lower latency for interactive summarization; we care about median 200ms per request for short drafts. How do we balance that with quality?
[03:46] Priya: We'll show a filtering example. On the Console, set latency band to <250ms and sequence-length profile to short/medium. The picklist will show model variants with measured tail and p50 latencies on H100 and A100. Then the Optimize module recommends quantization (int8 with 4-bit KV for example) or routing policies to fall back to a faster distill for short requests.
[04:15] [04:15] Daniel: Also you can set cost windows and we output estimated $/1k tokens given your traffic distribution — that helps weigh latency vs cost.
[04:27] Ethan: That cost estimate — is it accurate for dedicated pools?
[04:33] Daniel: For Dedicated we use committed capacity profiles and report amortized GPU cost plus per-token inference; it's an estimate but we include sensitivity bands. For private deployments on-prem, we provide configuration knobs but you run the final numbers locally.
[04:49] [screen walkthrough, longer pause]
[05:10] Priya: Here's an example picklist for a summarization workload. See Model-Alpha-v2, it shows quality 87 (catalog bench), workload bench 89 on your reference dataset. It flags that Model-Alpha-v2 needs 30GB GPU memory and runs well on H100 with int8 quant.
[05:33] Marta: We like Model-Alpha's precision but worried about hallucination on legal docs. Do you surface hallucination metrics?
[05:41] Priya: We run targeted hallucination suites and show regression alerts tied to prompt sets in Optimize. You can pin prompt evals and have automatic rollback if hallucination increases.
[05:54] Samir: Can we add our own eval tasks to the compatibility matrix?
[05:58] Priya: Yes — we ingest your eval suite and show workload-level scores alongside catalog scores. That's what we do in bench sprints.
[06:08] [06:08] Ethan: About benchmarks — how long does a sprint take? We have a small team and can't block lots of infra.
[06:16] Priya: Typical bench sprint is 3–5 business days for initial shortlist testing (3–5 models). End-to-end with integration and a second pass it's 1–2 weeks. We try to parallelize runs and cache common results to reduce cost.
[06:30] Marta: And what resources do you need from us?
[06:33] Priya: A small sample dataset (anonymized), a priors prompt set, and a CI hook if you want automation. Optionally, a contact in infra for VPN/VPC details if you pursue Private.
[06:47] [06:47] Priyanka: For compliance we asked about audit log retention and which events are logged.
[06:53] Alex: We log token-level events as well as model selection decisions, rollouts, and API key changes. In Private you control retention. In Hosted we keep 90 days by default for audit logs, with add-on retention.
[07:10] [screen change]
[07:20] Daniel: Now a quick demo of the API integration pattern. You can call /v1/generate with route=cp-summarize-route. The route resolves to a model alias that maps to a weighted pool — for example 80% Model-Alpha-v2, 20% distill for bursts. We also support streaming and tool/function calling for structured output.
[07:50] Ethan: Does streaming work with KV cache and long context?
[07:56] Priya: Yes. Streaming is orthogonal — we flush tokens as generated while still maintaining KV cache on the backend. It's supported in both Hosted and Dedicated.
[08:06] [08:06] Samir: Suppose we start on Hosted and later move to Dedicated — what changes in the integration?
[08:13] Daniel: Minimal code changes — primarily you update the route endpoint to point to your dedicated namespace and swap credentials. The Console migrator helps export routing and rollout configs.
[08:25] [08:25] Marta: Good. Cost control is important — can Redwood tell us where tokens are being spent in the stack?
[08:32] Alex: The Console has a token-level cost breakdown, including model, routing, and caching delta. Optimize will surface caches to enable prefix reuse and suggest batching policies.
[08:44] [08:44] Priya: A quick note on batching: continuous batching can reduce per-token cost but increases p95 latency. Optimize recommends batch sizes per route based on your latency SLO and traffic distribution.
[09:01] [09:01] Priyanka: On encryption — do you support customer-managed keys for embeddings storage?
[09:07] Alex: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can use your KMS for data at rest encryption; embeddings store can be configured to use HSM-backed keys.
[09:17] [09:17] Samir: Are there any known incompatibilities for LLaMA-derived open models when running on int8? We've seen instability in KV.
[09:26] Priya: Good point — some LLaMA forks need specific kernel paths. We maintain kernel compatibility flags in the matrix. For certain models we recommend FP16 or 4-bit KV tweaks; Optimize will suggest those automatically if the workload triggers instability.
[09:44] [09:44] Marta: Can you show a compatibility matrix snippet that compares three shortlisted models?
[09:50] [screen share]
[09:55] Priya: Here's a matrix: columns are model, p50 latency, p95, med quality, hallucination-score, kv-efficiency, recommended quant. Model-Alpha-v2 (p50 180ms, p95 320ms, quality 89, halluc 4%), Model-Beta-7B (p50 120ms, p95 240ms, quality 81, halluc 7%, recommended int8), Model-Gamma-LT (p50 220ms, p95 450ms, quality 92, halluc 3%, needs FP16).
[10:31] Ethan: That helps. For our mixed traffic, would you recommend routing by size or by latency?
[10:37] Priya: You can use smart routing: size-based for long docs (Gamma) and latency for short drafts (Beta distill). Also set automatic fallback when p95 > threshold to route to a cheaper/fast variant.
[10:51] [10:51] Samir: Any examples of customers who moved from Hosted to Dedicated and the lift/cost delta?
[10:58] Alex: We have a case study (link in follow-up) — typical improvement is 20–40% cost reduction at scale with better p50 stability, but it depends on utilization and burst patterns.
[11:12] [11:12] Marta: Let's talk next steps. We're keen to run a bench sprint on three models with our dataset, and we'd like security docs.
[11:20] Alex: Sounds good. Proposed plan: 1) redact samples and share a small evaluation dataset; 2) Redwood runs a 5-day bench sprint and returns compatibility matrix + cost estimate; 3) schedule a deep-dive on day 3 for preliminary results.
[11:36] Priyanka: We'll need SOC2 + encryption docs before handing over anonymized samples.
[11:41] Alex: We'll attach those to the follow-up email.
[11:46] [11:46] Daniel: Also we'll include a sample API integration snippet and a Console export of route config.
[11:52] Marta: Timeline — we want pilot in 6 weeks. Is that achievable?
[11:56] Priya: Yes, 6 weeks is doable: bench sprint + integration + small pilot on Hosted or Dedicated depending on security decision.
[12:07] [12:07] Samir: One last technical — do you expose kernel-level tuning suggestions per model? We sometimes need to tune for long-window sparse attention.
[12:15] Priya: We include kernel mapping notes in the matrix — e.g., recommended cuBLAS/cuDNN flags or attention kernel variants. For Private we can share further low-level tuning docs.
[12:30] [12:30] Alex: Alright, recap and next steps in the last 90 seconds: Redwood sends security pack + SOC2, sample route export, and pricing/committed capacity options. You send anonymized sample dataset and confirm who will be the bench sprint contact.
[12:48] Marta: Thanks all, that was helpful.
[12:51] Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the plan and calendar invite for the bench sprint kickoff.
[12:58] [call ends]
